rule.summary: At the unhandled stage, after the GUI, FabricSurface marks a mouse button (wheel and wheel release included), a screen touch or the mouse Godot emulates from a touch (device -1) as handled when ApplicationRuntime::claims, which runs physical_hit_test for that Surface at the event's point, finds a View (tag other than 0). Motion and drag are not claimed.

decisions: The rule: at the unhandled stage the Surface claims a mouse button, a touch or the emulated mouse when React Native's hit test finds a View at the event's point; the empty area (the box-none root) stays the world's.

The decision is by hit test and not by handler, as React Native on a phone decides by geometry, pointerEvents and hitSlop (iOS RCTViewComponentView.mm 114-124, 362-368, 772-785; Android TouchTargetHelper.kt 252-270, 327-402).
The claim runs after the GUI, so the Controls of Godot's GUI that React Native mounts (Button, LineEdit, Switch) keep their events; the before-gui sabotage proves it with the fixture's Switch.
hit_test, apply_pointer_filters, input() and wheel() are unchanged; a2 adds a public method and an override.
The Surface relies on the unhandled order: it is called before the world only when the HUD's CanvasLayer comes after the world in the tree. The probe asserts it with a witness.
Motion and drag are outside the rule and are recorded as informative rows.
The wheel over a tree overlay is normative from a2 (L6); the Modal holds on every host.
views-ignore now fails 5 named checks (the Switch click and tap, three hovers) instead of 21: with the claim the hit test still finds a View whose Control is IGNORE.

goNoGo.reading: Slice 2 of 3. On the numbers of slices 1 and 2 the pointer reaches exactly one side by the rule of a phone: 0 of 100 leaks in the six gaps, 100 of 100 for the world in the empty area, with the controls and sabotages rejecting every way of getting it wrong, headless in two topologies and in a real macOS window in one. The go/no-go itself is decided in slice 3, which has to weigh what stays open: motion, hover and drag, a HUD before the world, and the lack of a phone or a hardware pointer.
goNoGo.timeBox: 3 slices: 1 = the policy a1 and what it leaves open; 2 = this one; 3 = the decision.

open: Pointer motion, hover and drag are not claimed: over a place the GUI lets through the world still hears the motion (20 of 20) and a drag that starts there (20 drags and 20 emulated motions, with the touch and its emulated mouse claimed).
A release away from its press follows the point of the release.
A HUD placed before the world in the tree, a HUD of several layers, other cameras and several windows are not measured.
Hardware pointers, a real touch screen, multi-touch and mobile exports; the iphone criterion of V05-02 stays open (package P7).
limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI is pending.
The events are synthetic, delivered through Input.parse_input_event: no hardware pointer, no real touch screen, no multi-touch (a second finger), no real drag.
No Godot mobile export and no iPhone run.
The counts are exact and say nothing about latency or frame time. The windowed lane's frames ran unpaced (the display was asleep) and it makes no frame-time claim.
The scene has the world before the HUD's CanvasLayer in the tree and a Camera2D at (384, 256) with zoom 2; other arrangements are not measured.
The pre-a1 control is a rebuild on the current main, not the binary of slice 1.
